the HLA- DR locus contains at least two different genes, that the HLA-DQ locus contains at least one, and that the HLA class II genes are subject to regulation at the level of transcription, RNA processing, and protein stability.

the regulation of HLA class II expression.
the regulation of the expression and the structure of HLA class II genes.
the molecular genetics of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC), the gene complex in vertebrates that controls the immune response.

HLA- DR is a highly regulated gene product, with multiple levels of control, both transcriptional and posttranscriptional.

the mutations in this study have revealed the existence of several distinct mechanisms that regulate HLA-DR expression, some of which are shared by the mouse and some of which have no natural counterparts.

HLA class II structure and expression can be affected by mutations that have not been found in natural mutants.

the mutations in the HLA class II gene that have been isolated to date are similar to those that occur naturally and that they have provided a powerful set of tools for the analysis of the structure and function of HLA class II molecules.

the HLA class II region is very sensitive to mutagenesis.
